edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. I, 1

source_text: Quomodo didicimus per Moysen esse quaedam non solum sancta, sed et sancta sanctorum, et alia non tantum sabbata, sed et sabbata sabbatorum, sic nunc quoque docemur scribente Solomone esse quaedam non solum cantica, sed et cantica canticorum. Beatus quidem et is, qui ingreditur in sancta, sed multo ille beatior, qui ingreditur in sancta sanctorum. Beatus, qui sabbata sabbatizat, sed beatior, qui sabbatizat sabbata sabbatorum. Beatus similiter et is, qui intellegit cantica et canit ea — nemo quippe nisi in sollemnitatibus canit —, sed multo beatior qui canit cantica canticorum. Et sicut is, qui ingreditur in sancta, pluribus adhuc indiget, ut valeat introire in sancta sanctorum, et qui sabbatum celebrat, quod a Deo populo constitutum est, multa adhuc necessaria habet, ut agat sabbatum sabbatorum, eodem modo difficile repperitur, qui omnia, quae in scripturis continentur, cantica peragrans valeat adscendere ad cantica canticorum. Egredi oportet ex Aegypto et egressum de terra Aegypti pertransire mare rubrum, ut possis primum canticum canere dicens: Cantemus Domino; gloriose enim magnificatus est. Licet autem primum dixeris canticum, adhuc longe es a cantico canticorum. Perambula terram deserti spiritaliter, donec venias ad puteum, quem foderunt reges, ut ibi secundum canticum canas. Post haec veni ad viciniam sanctae terrae, ut super Iordanis ripam constitutus cantes canticum Moysi dicens: Attende caelum, et loquar; et audiat terra verba oris mei. Rursum habes necessarium, ut milites sub Iesu et terram sanctam hereditate possideas et apis tibi prophetet apisque te iudicet — Debbora quippe apis interpretatur —, ut possis et illud carmen, quod in Iudicum libro continetur, edicere. Ad Regnorum deinceps volumen adscendens veni ad canticum, quando David fugit de manu omnium inimicorum suorum et de manu Saul et dixit: Dominus, firmamentum meum et fortitudo mea et refugium meum et liberator meus. Perveniendum tibi est ad Esaiam, ut cum illo dicas: Cantabo canticum dilecto vineae meae. Et cum universa transieris, ad altiora conscende, ut possis anima decora cum sponso et hoc canere canticum canticorum. Quod ex quot personis constet, incertus sum. Orantibus autem vobis et revelante Deo quattuor in his mihi videor invenire personas, virum et sponsam, cum sponsa adulescentulas, cum sponso sodalium greges. Alia dicuntur a sponsa, alia a sponso, nonnulla a iuveneculis, quaedam a sodalibus sponsi. Congruum quippe est, ut in nuptiis adulescentularum sit multitudo cum sponsa, iuvenum turba cum sponso. Haec omnia noli foris quaerere, noli extra eos, qui praedicatione evangelii sunt salvati. Christum sponsum intellege, ecclesiam sponsam sine macula et ruga, de qua scriptum est: ut exhiberet sibi gloriosam ecclesiam non habentem maculam neque rugam aut aliud quid eorum, sed ut sit sancta et immaculata. Eos vero, qui, cum sint fideles, non sunt tamen istiusmodi, quales sermo praefatus est, sed iuxta modum quendam adepti videntur salutem, animas animadverte credentium et adulescentulas esse cum sponsa. Angelos vero et eos, qui pervenerunt in virum perfectum, intellege viros esse cum sponso. Vide igitur mihi quattuor ordines, unum et unam, duos choros inter se concinnentes, sponsam canere cum iuveneculis, sponsum canere cum sociis. Et cum haec intellexeris, audi canticum canticorum et festina intellegere illud et cum sponsa dicere ea, quae sponsa dicit, ut audias, quae audivit et sponsa. Si autem non potueris dicere cum sponsa, quae dixit sponsa, ut audias ea, quae dicta sunt sponsae, festina vel cum sponsi sodalibus fieri. Porro si et illis inferior es, esto cum adulescentulis, quae in sponsae deliciis commorantur. Haec quippe in hoc libro, fabula pariter et epithalamio, sunt personae; ex quo et gentiles sibi epithalamium vindicarunt et istius generis carmen assumptum est, epithalamium siquidem est canticum canticorum. Primum sponsa orat et statim in mediis precibus auditur. Videt praesentem sponsum, videt adulescentulas suo comitatui copulatas. Deinde respondet ei sponsus et post sponsi eloquia, dum ille pro eius patitur salute, respondent sodales, donec sponsus sit in recubitu et a passione consurgat, se quaedam sponsae ornamenta facturos.
pass_a_gloss: In what way we-learned through Moses there-are certain-things not only holy but also holy-of-holies, and other-things not only sabbaths but also sabbaths-of-sabbaths, so now also we-are-taught with-Solomon writing there-are certain-things not only songs but also song-of-songs. Blessed indeed also he who enters into holy-things, but much that-one more-blessed who enters into holy-of-holies... [ascent through Exodus song, well-song, Deuteronomy, Judges/Deborah, Kingdoms/David, Isaiah vineyard-song, then Song of Songs]. Four persons: man/bridegroom and bride; with bride young-women; with bridegroom companion-flocks. Christ=bridegroom; church=bride without spot/wrinkle (Eph 5). Faithful-but-lesser = young women; angels and perfect-man = men with bridegroom. Prefer speak as bride; else companions; else young women. Book = story and wedding-song (epithalamium). Bride prays, is heard mid-prayer; sees bridegroom and young women; bridegroom answers; companions will make ornaments while he is on couch until rising from passion.
notes: Pass A literalist gloss ≠ Pass B literary English.
Song lemma sense-checked against Baehrens; Lawson ACW not used for wording.
pass_b_english: How we have learned through Moses that there are things not only holy, but [[holy of holies >> Bible:Exodus 26:33]], and others not only sabbaths, but sabbaths of sabbaths — so now too we are taught, Solomon writing, that there are songs not only songs, but a [[Song of Songs >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:1]]. Blessed indeed is the one who enters the holy place; far more blessed the one who enters the holy of holies. Blessed is the one who keeps sabbaths; more blessed the one who keeps the [[sabbath of sabbaths >> Bible:Leviticus 16:31]]. Blessed likewise is the one who understands the songs and sings them — for no one sings except on feast days — yet far more blessed is the one who sings the Song of Songs. And just as the one who enters the holy place still needs many things before he can go into the holy of holies, and the one who keeps the sabbath God appointed for the people still needs much before he can keep the sabbath of sabbaths, so it is hard to find anyone who, passing through all the songs contained in the Scriptures, can rise to the Song of Songs. You must go out from Egypt, and once you have gone out from the land of Egypt you must cross the Red Sea, so that you can sing the first song: [[Let us sing to the Lord, for he is gloriously magnified >> Bible:Exodus 15:1]]. Yet even if you have sung the first song, you are still far from the [[Song of Songs >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:1]]. Walk the desert land in the spirit until you come to the well that kings dug, and there sing the second song. After that draw near the holy land, and standing on the bank of the Jordan sing Moses’ song: [[Give ear, O heaven, and I will speak >> Bible:Deuteronomy 32:1]]; and let the earth hear the words of my mouth. Again you must take the land under Jesus as soldiers and inherit the holy land, and let the bee prophesy to you and judge you — for Deborah is interpreted “bee” — so that you may also utter the song that stands in the book of Judges. Climbing next into the volume of Kingdoms, come to the song when David fled from the hand of all his enemies and from the hand of Saul and said: [[The Lord is my firmament and my strength >> Bible:2 Samuel 22:2]] and my refuge and my deliverer. You must reach Isaiah, so that with him you may say: [[I will sing a song to my beloved of his vineyard >> Bible:Isaiah 5:1]]. And when you have passed through all these, climb higher still, so that as a soul made fair you may sing with the Bridegroom this Song of Songs. Of how many persons it is composed I am not sure. Yet as you pray and God reveals, I seem to find four persons in it: the Bridegroom and the Bride; with the Bride, young women; with the Bridegroom, companies of companions. Some things are said by the Bride, some by the Bridegroom, some by the young women, some by the Bridegroom’s companions. It is fitting that at a wedding there should be a throng of young women with the Bride and a crowd of young men with the Bridegroom. Do not look for any of this outside those who have been saved by the preaching of the gospel. Understand Christ as the Bridegroom, and the Church as the Bride without spot or wrinkle, of whom it is written that he might present to himself a glorious Church, [[not having spot or wrinkle >> Bible:Ephesians 5:27]] or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without blemish. Those who are faithful yet are not of that sort the word has just described, but have somehow attained a measure of salvation — mark them as believing souls, the young women with the Bride. Angels, and those who have come to the perfect man, understand as the men with the Bridegroom. See then four orders for me: the one and the one, and two choirs answering each other — the Bride singing with the young women, the Bridegroom singing with his companions. And when you have understood this, hear the [[Song of Songs >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:1]], and hasten to understand it, and to say with the Bride what the Bride says, so that you may hear what the Bride too has heard. But if you cannot say with the Bride what the Bride said, so as to hear what is spoken to the Bride, hasten at least to be among the Bridegroom’s companions. And if you are still beneath even them, be with the young women who linger in the Bride’s delights. For these are the persons in this book, which is at once a story and a wedding-song; from it the nations too claimed an epithalamium for themselves, and a poem of this kind was taken up — for an epithalamium is what the Song of Songs is. First the Bride prays, and at once in the midst of her prayers she is heard. She sees the Bridegroom present; she sees young women joined to her company. Then the Bridegroom answers her, and after the Bridegroom’s words, while he suffers for her salvation, the companions answer that until the Bridegroom is on his couch and rises from the passion they will make certain ornaments for the Bride.
